statusText: Green - the CME weekend halt covers twenty-one of the twenty-four published hours, holding Tail at the floor of a closed venue, while an official Saudi-led coalition statement closes the Yanbu question that was the main open ambiguity in the previous hour
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 4 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is the single hour in this window carrying elevated conditional risk, and is published with Tail 14, still inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: A Saudi-led coalition statement says the Houthi attack on Yanbu was thwarted, closing the weekend's main open ambiguity, while Japan's three-day Silver Week cash closure emerges as a verified liquidity qualifier for the 22:00Z futures restart
body: Twenty-one of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final three contain the restart and its first two hours. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September at 20:00Z, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z at 29,917.25 - up 0.59% from a 29,743.00 previous close but 76 points below its 29,993.25 session high, so the last observed futures mark was not a session extreme - and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run and are unchanged: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX settled 14.81, down 4.08%, at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The Fed H.15 release shows the 10-year at 4.94% and the 2-year at 4.67% for 17 September, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88% after the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, the first hike since 2023. WTI settled 100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent 103.87, down 0.91%. Two verified developments separate this hour from the last. The first resolves an ambiguity rather than adding an escalation. Coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki said defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired at Riyadh at dawn and that attacks on Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu were thwarted. The previous published hour flagged the unverified Houthi claim against Aramco facilities at Yanbu as the main open question in the evidence base; an official account now addresses it, and in a de-escalating direction. The qualification is that the official line and the visual record differ in emphasis - Saudi authorities reported no casualties or damage, while Reuters video carried by ABC News shows a fuel tank bearing the Aramco logo burning at a depot near King Khalid International Airport before being extinguished. What both accounts agree on is the part that matters for index risk: no reported casualties, and no reported interruption to production or export capacity. The impact sits at the fuel-distribution end, and Yanbu loadings have in any case been suspended since mid-September after the East-West pipeline attack. The standing counterweight is unchanged, with CENTCOM reporting Hormuz oil and LNG transits at a six-month high, and Friday's third consecutive down day in crude is consistent with that easing rather than with a supply shock. The second development is structural and new to this assessment. Japan's cash equity market is closed for three consecutive sessions - Monday 21 September for Respect for the Aged Day, Tuesday 22 September as a citizens' holiday and Wednesday 23 September for the Autumnal Equinox - as part of Silver Week, with JPX running derivatives holiday trading across those dates. That matters for the restart hours published here, because the Asian sessions immediately following the 22:00Z reopening will be missing their largest cash market. It is a liquidity qualifier, not a directional one: thinner cash depth can lengthen the time a weekend gap takes to be absorbed without implying which way it points, so it is scored into restart Stress and not into Tail. The shared cross-asset context file was collected at 23:40Z and is about 105 minutes old at this assessment, past the 90-minute freshness limit, so it is treated as stale and excluded from this run entirely; the research above is fully independent of it. One scheduled item is named for completeness: Monday's effective Nasdaq-100 rebalance lifts the SpaceX weight to about 2.82% from roughly 1.28%, but the $15.5-22 billion of mechanical passive buying executed in Friday's closing cross rather than at the restart, so the flow sits behind the market. A Trump-Xi summit is widely reported for 24 September, but the time remains unscheduled, so it is omitted from the verified event calendar and named only as a week-ahead checkpoint. Tail is held at 4, the floor of a closed venue, because the current hour offers no mechanism for mean reversion to fail and none of the overlay's amplifiers - shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, extreme-holding, aligned cross-assets - can even be observed without an open tape. Stress is held at 26: the Yanbu resolution removes some unpriced headline weight while the Japan closure adds an equivalent amount of restart-liquidity concern, and the two offset. Confidence improves one point to 74 because an official account has closed the weekend's main open question and every Friday mark was re-verified at primary sources, tempered by the loss of the stale shared context and by the gap between the official and visual damage descriptions.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 for twenty-one slots before stepping down to 4 across the final three hours. Stress opened at 25, decayed to a 21 plateau across five midday hours, then drifted back through 22, 23 and 24 before reaching 26 in the closing hour of the window. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence fell steadily from 83 to 72 as distance from the Friday tape grew, recovered to 74 once the Riyadh damage picture was corroborated across independent outlets, and settled at 73 in the closing hour.
outlookSummary: Twenty-one of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final three contain the restart and its first two hours. Cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z, and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday. No scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside the window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 4 through the deepest part of the halt, steps to 5 from 05:00Z, 6 from 08:00Z, 7 from 10:00Z, 8 from 13:00Z, 9 from 16:00Z, 10 from 19:00Z and 11 at 21:00Z, then reaches 14 across the restart and its first full hour before easing to 13 - a drift that tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure. The one genuinely observable checkpoint inside the halt is Saudi Arabia's Tadawul session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z, the first market-based read on the Riyadh depot fire now that the coalition has described the Yanbu attack as thwarted. The 22:00Z reopening auction remains the single hour carrying real conditional risk, and this run adds a verified qualifier to it: Japan's cash equity market is shut Monday through Wednesday for Silver Week, so the Asian sessions following the restart will be unusually thin, which lifts restart Stress without implying direction. That hour is published conditionally as event/whipsaw with no opening structure yet observed. Monday's effective Nasdaq-100 rebalance is named as a checkpoint, but its mechanical flow concentrated in Friday's closing cross. Every published hour maps to EA_ON and no danger window is identified.
